name: Tamara
desc: Buy now pay later fintech letting shoppers split online and in-store purchases into instalments at partner merchants.
markets: Consumers and merchants in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf markets such as the UAE and Kuwait.
rationale: Gulf consumer brand with heavy marketing; Saudi and Gulf race hospitality and fan activation could support customer growth.

name: Uber Technologies
desc: Operates ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery and freight platforms connecting consumers, drivers, couriers, merchants and shippers.
markets: Operates in roughly 70 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Global consumer mobility brand; F1 race-city audiences and hospitality fit ride-hailing, Uber Eats and autonomous mobility messaging.

name: X (formerly Twitter)
desc: Social network for short posts, video and live conversation, earning from advertising and Premium subscriptions.
markets: Users and advertisers worldwide, with largest audiences in the US, Japan, India and Europe.
rationale: Global real-time sports conversation platform; content and media partnership possible, but advertiser caution and ownership controversy weigh.
changed: Acquired by Elon Musk in 2022 and delisted; merged with xAI in 2025, which became a SpaceX subsidiary in 2026

name: Noon
desc: Online marketplace selling electronics, fashion, groceries and household goods, with quick-commerce, food delivery and Namshi fashion.
markets: Customers in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Egypt; no verified expansion beyond these markets.
rationale: Heavily advertised Gulf consumer brand backed by PIF; Saudi and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix offer regional activation.

name: Snap Inc.
desc: Develops Snapchat messaging app, augmented reality Lenses and Spectacles glasses, earning mainly from advertising and subscriptions.
markets: Users worldwide, strongest in North America, Europe, India and the Middle East.
rationale: Young global audience and AR technology suit F1 fan content and sponsor activations aimed at younger viewers.

name: Virtu Financial
desc: Electronic market maker providing liquidity across equities, fixed income, currencies and commodities, plus execution and analytics services.
markets: Trades on venues across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; institutional clients worldwide.
rationale: Institutional brand with low public profile; B2B hospitality possible but marketing need is limited.
changed: Acquired ITG in 2019

name: Kakao
desc: South Korean internet group running KakaoTalk messenger plus payments, banking, mobility, entertainment, music and commerce services.
markets: Mainly South Korea, with some entertainment and content businesses abroad; limited international scale.
rationale: Dominant Korean consumer platform, but F1 has a small Korean following; weak-to-moderate fit unless targeting global content.

name: Atome
desc: Buy now pay later and consumer credit app letting shoppers pay in instalments at partner merchants.
markets: Consumers and merchants in Southeast Asian markets such as Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines.
rationale: Regional consumer fintech; Singapore Grand Prix could support brand building in Southeast Asia, though budget may be limited.

name: Experian
desc: Provides credit reports and scores, fraud prevention, data analytics and marketing services to lenders, businesses and consumers.
markets: Operates in about 30 countries, largest in North America, UK, Brazil, plus Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global B2B data brand with consumer credit products; F1 hospitality and data-analytics storytelling could reach lenders and consumers.

name: Databricks
desc: Data and AI platform for enterprises to store, process and analyse data and build AI applications.
markets: Enterprise customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Enterprise AI brand competing with F1-sponsoring tech firms; data-and-AI showcase and B2B hospitality give strong fit.

name: Kuaishou Technology
desc: Operates Kuaishou short-video and live-streaming app, Kwai abroad, e-commerce, and the Kling AI video generation model.
markets: Mainly China; Kwai app serves users in Brazil, other Latin American markets and the Middle East.
rationale: Large consumer platform; Shanghai Grand Prix and Kwai in Brazil offer content and fan-engagement angles.

name: Nebius Group
desc: Provides GPU cloud computing and AI infrastructure services to AI developers and enterprises from its own data centres.
markets: Customers in Europe and the US, with data centre capacity in Finland, France and the US; offices in Israel.
rationale: Fast-growing AI infrastructure supplier; technology showcase and B2B hospitality could support enterprise sales in Europe and US.
changed: Renamed from Yandex N.V. to Nebius Group in 2024 after selling its Russian businesses

name: Orange S.A.
desc: Telecom operator providing mobile, broadband, TV and enterprise network services to consumers, businesses and governments.
markets: France, Spain, Poland, Belgium and other European markets, plus Africa and the Middle East; Orange Business serves multinationals.
rationale: Major consumer and enterprise brand with sports sponsorship culture; French and European fans plus B2B connectivity showcase.

name: SpaceX Super Intelligence (SpaceXAI)
desc: Develops the Grok AI models and chatbot and, through subsidiaries, operates the X social network and Cursor.
markets: Grok and X users worldwide; enterprise and developer customers internationally.
rationale: High-profile AI brand with global consumer reach; tech showcase possible, but controversy and parent priorities make fit uncertain.
changed: Founded as xAI in 2023; merged with X in 2025; became a SpaceX subsidiary in February 2026

name: Super Micro Computer (Supermicro)
desc: Designs and manufactures servers, storage and rack-scale systems, especially GPU-based AI servers, for data centres and cloud providers.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia; manufacturing in the US, Taiwan and Netherlands.
rationale: AI hardware supplier competing with F1-sponsoring HPE and Dell; technology tie-in and B2B hospitality could help.

name: Telefonica
desc: Telecom operator providing mobile, broadband, TV and business connectivity under Movistar, O2 and Vivo brands.
markets: Spain, Germany, the UK through Virgin Media O2, Brazil and other Latin American markets.
rationale: Strong Spanish-speaking and Brazilian consumer brands; Madrid Grand Prix from 2026 and São Paulo race give activation options.

name: Capgemini
desc: IT services and consulting group offering digital transformation, cloud, data, AI, engineering and outsourcing to large organisations.
markets: Operates in about 50 countries across Europe, North America, India and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Rivals such as Cognizant, Globant and Akkodis sponsor F1; engineering and AI showcase plus hospitality fit well.
changed: Acquired WNS in 2025

name: FICO (Fair Isaac Corporation)
desc: Analytics software company behind the FICO credit score, plus decisioning and fraud detection software for lenders.
markets: Mainly US lenders and consumers; software clients in Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: US-centric B2B and consumer score brand; F1's US growth gives some hospitality value but no obvious tie-in.

name: Jefferies Financial Group
desc: Investment bank and financial services group offering advisory, capital markets, trading and asset management to institutions.
markets: Clients and offices in the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Investment bank rivals such as Goldman Sachs and UBS use F1 hospitality; client entertainment value is clear.

name: Ramp
desc: Provides corporate cards, expense management, bill payments and accounting automation software to US businesses.
markets: Business customers in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Fast-growing US B2B fintech; F1's US races and audience growth suit brand building with business decision-makers.

name: TELUS
desc: Telecom company providing mobile, internet, TV and security services, plus TELUS Health and TELUS Digital businesses.
markets: Core telecom customers in Canada; TELUS Health and TELUS Digital serve clients internationally.
rationale: Strong Canadian consumer brand; Canadian Grand Prix offers domestic activation and hospitality.

name: MoonPay
desc: Crypto payments company letting people buy, sell and swap digital assets, and embedding on-ramps into wallets and exchanges.
markets: Consumers and partner platforms across North America, Europe and other regions where licensed.
rationale: Crypto rivals such as Crypto.com, OKX and Kraken sponsor F1; MoonPay already uses celebrity and sports marketing.

name: Medtronic
desc: Makes cardiac, diabetes, surgical, neuromodulation, spine and vascular medical devices sold to hospitals and health systems.
markets: Sells in more than 150 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Global healthcare brand; F1 engineering and performance themes are a stretch, mainly B2B hospitality value.

name: Anysphere (Cursor)
desc: Develops Cursor, an AI coding agent and code editor sold by subscription to developers and enterprises.
markets: Individual developers and enterprise software teams worldwide, across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: AI developer tool with global reach; technology showcase possible, but marketing decisions now sit with parent SpaceXAI.
changed: Now a subsidiary of SpaceXAI (SpaceX), per Wikipedia; previously independent

name: Unity Software
desc: Provides the Unity real-time 3D engine and advertising and monetisation tools for game and app developers.
markets: Developers and studios across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Real-time 3D and simulation technology could showcase in F1 fan and digital experiences; moderate fit.
changed: Merged with ironSource in 2022

name: WiseTech Global
desc: Develops CargoWise logistics software used by freight forwarders, customs brokers and logistics providers to run operations.
markets: Logistics customers in many countries across Asia-Pacific, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Global B2B software for logistics, where DHL and DP World sponsor F1; logistics tie-in but limited brand marketing.
changed: Acquired e2open in 2025

name: Stats Perform
desc: Supplies sports data, AI analytics, video and content, including Opta, to media, teams, leagues and betting operators.
markets: Media, sports and betting customers worldwide, with major operations in the UK and US.
rationale: Sports data supplier; partnership more likely as data or technology supplier than sponsor; B2B visibility to sports buyers.
changed: Formed by the 2019 merger of STATS and Perform Group; owned by Vista Equity Partners

name: Wayflyer
desc: Provides revenue-based financing and analytics to e-commerce brands for inventory and marketing spend.
markets: E-commerce merchants in the US, UK, Europe, Canada and Australia.
rationale: Niche B2B fintech with limited marketing scale; F1 reaches e-commerce founders only indirectly, so weak-to-moderate fit.

name: AlphaSense
desc: AI market intelligence platform searching filings, transcripts, broker research and expert calls for investors and corporations.
markets: Clients in North America, Europe and Asia among investment firms and corporates.
rationale: Customers include banks and corporates entertained at F1; B2B hospitality value, limited consumer need.
changed: Acquired Tegus in 2024

name: Autodesk
desc: Sells design and engineering software such as AutoCAD, Revit, Maya and Fusion to architects, engineers and manufacturers.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific through direct and reseller channels.
rationale: Design and engineering software used in motorsport; technology showcase competes with Siemens and Synopsys (Ansys) in F1.

name: Canva
desc: Online design platform with templates and AI tools for presentations, social posts, video, documents and print.
markets: Users in about 190 countries, with large bases in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Mass consumer and business brand; F1 content creation, team design tools and global audience make a plausible fit.

name: Nuro
desc: Develops autonomous driving software, the Nuro Driver, licensed to automakers and mobility companies for robotaxis and delivery.
markets: Operations and testing in the United States; partners include Uber and Lucid; no confirmed overseas operations.
rationale: Autonomous driving technology fits automotive themes; small B2B licensing business with limited marketing budget.
changed: Shifted from building delivery vehicles to licensing its driving software in 2024

name: OpenText
desc: Enterprise information management software company selling content management, cybersecurity, analytics and AI products to enterprises and governments.
markets: Enterprise and government customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Enterprise software and cybersecurity peers sponsor F1 heavily; data-management showcase and hospitality give reasonable fit.
changed: Acquired Micro Focus in 2023

name: SentinelOne
desc: Cybersecurity company selling its AI-based Singularity platform for endpoint, cloud and identity protection to organisations.
markets: Business and government customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Rivals CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Bitdefender sponsor F1; strong precedent for security brand technology showcase.

name: Tabby
desc: Buy now pay later fintech offering instalment payments, cards and a shopping app to Gulf consumers.
markets: Consumers and merchants in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Kuwait; Saudi IPO reported as planned.
rationale: Heavily advertised Gulf brand; Saudi and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix offer strong regional activation.
changed: Moved headquarters from the UAE to Riyadh

name: Thomson Reuters
desc: Provides legal, tax and accounting software and information such as Westlaw, plus the Reuters news agency.
markets: Professional and corporate customers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Reuters is a global news brand; B2B hospitality for law and accounting firms is the main angle.

name: Match Group
desc: Online dating company operating Tinder, Hinge, Match, OkCupid, Plenty of Fish, Meetic and Azar apps.
markets: Users across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Tinder and Hinge target young adults, a growing F1 demographic; consumer brand activation fit is plausible.
changed: Spun off from IAC in 2020

name: AppLovin
desc: Mobile and e-commerce advertising technology company whose AI ad engine matches advertisers with app inventory.
markets: Advertisers and publishers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Ad-tech brand with little consumer marketing need; B2B profile-building possible but fit is moderate.
changed: Sold its mobile games business to Tripledot in 2025

name: Celonis
desc: Process mining and process intelligence software helping large enterprises analyse and improve business operations.
markets: Enterprise customers in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific; co-headquarters in New York.
rationale: Enterprise software peers such as SAP and ServiceNow sponsor F1; process-optimisation story and hospitality suit it.

name: Check Point Software Technologies
desc: Cybersecurity company selling firewalls, cloud, endpoint, email and threat prevention products to businesses and governments.
markets: Over 100,000 organisations across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions; US office in Redwood City.
rationale: Cybersecurity rivals sponsor F1 widely; security showcase and B2B hospitality give strong fit.

name: S&P Global
desc: Provides credit ratings, market data, benchmarks such as the S&P 500, and commodity and mobility intelligence.
markets: Investors, banks, corporates and governments across all major regions.
rationale: Global financial-markets brand; B2B hospitality for institutional clients and automotive data tie-in through Mobility.
changed: Merged with IHS Markit in 2022

name: CDW Corporation
desc: Resells hardware, software and IT services from major vendors to business, government, education and healthcare customers.
markets: Customers in the United States, United Kingdom and Canada.
rationale: IT reseller already active in US motorsport; F1's US races and vendor co-marketing give moderate fit.

name: CGI Inc.
desc: IT and business consulting firm offering systems integration, managed IT and software to governments and large enterprises.
markets: Clients in about 40 countries across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Rival IT services firms such as Cognizant and DXC sponsor F1; hospitality and technology showcase fit.

name: Saviynt
desc: Provides a cloud identity security platform for identity governance, access management and privileged access.
markets: Enterprise and government customers mainly in North America, with operations in Europe and India.
rationale: Cybersecurity peers sponsor F1; KKR-backed growth company could use hospitality, but brand scale is modest.

name: Safaricom
desc: Mobile network operator offering voice, data, broadband and M-Pesa mobile money services to consumers and businesses.
markets: Customers in Kenya and Ethiopia; no verified wider expansion.
rationale: Dominant East African brand, but F1 has no African race and little local following; weak fit.

name: Spotify
desc: Audio streaming service offering music, podcasts and audiobooks through free ad-supported and paid subscription tiers.
markets: Users in about 180 markets across all major regions.
rationale: Global consumer brand with football sponsorship experience; F1's young audience and music tie-ins give strong fit.

name: BT Group
desc: Telecom group providing broadband, mobile, TV and network services under BT, EE, Plusnet and Openreach.
markets: Consumers mainly in the UK; BT Business serves multinational enterprise customers worldwide.
rationale: Strong UK consumer brand; British Grand Prix and UK fan base give a domestic activation case.

name: Palantir Technologies
desc: Develops data integration and AI software such as Gotham, Foundry and AIP for governments and enterprises.
markets: Government and commercial customers in the US, UK, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Enterprise AI brand with strong profile; data and AI showcase fits F1, though defence work limits some partners.
changed: Moved headquarters from Denver to Miami

name: GoDaddy
desc: Domain registrar and web services company selling hosting, website builders, email and commerce tools to small businesses.
markets: Small-business customers in the US and many international markets across Europe, Asia and Latin America.
rationale: Heavy-advertising consumer brand with motorsport sponsorship history; F1 reaches small-business owners in US and abroad.

name: Harvey
desc: Generative AI platform for law firms and professional services firms to draft, review and research legal documents.
markets: Law firms and corporate legal teams in the US, UK, Europe and other markets.
rationale: Law firms such as Ashurst and Morrison Foerster sponsor F1; B2B hospitality could reach legal buyers.

name: Walgreens Boots Alliance
desc: Former holding company of the Walgreens and Boots pharmacy chains and Alliance Healthcare, now taken private.
markets: Walgreens stores in the US and Boots stores in the UK and Europe; holding company no longer listed.
rationale: Holding company no longer exists; approach Walgreens or Boots directly, whose US and UK consumer reach is large.
changed: Taken private by Sycamore Partners in 2025 and delisted from Nasdaq; Wikipedia describes the holding company as defunct

name: Applied Intuition
desc: Provides simulation, validation and vehicle software for automakers and autonomy programmes, including defence customers.
markets: Automaker and defence customers in the US, Europe, Japan and South Korea.
rationale: Vehicle software and simulation fit F1 engineering themes; B2B hospitality for automotive executives.

name: Deel
desc: HR and payroll platform helping companies hire, pay and manage employees and contractors in many countries.
markets: Business customers and their workers in more than 150 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Global HR brand like F1 sponsors UKG and Workday; international audience and hospitality fit.

name: Docusign
desc: Software company selling electronic signature and agreement management products to businesses by subscription.
markets: Business customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Well-known B2B brand with marketing budget; enterprise software peers sponsor F1, giving moderate-to-strong fit.

name: Keysight Technologies
desc: Makes electronic test and measurement equipment and design software for telecom, automotive, aerospace and semiconductor customers.
markets: Telecom, automotive and electronics customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Engineering-focused brand; electronics and automotive testing gives technology tie-in, but limited consumer marketing.
changed: Spun off from Agilent in 2014; acquired Spirent Communications in 2025

name: Mavenir
desc: Develops cloud-native mobile network software, including 5G core, voice, messaging and Open RAN, for telecom operators.
markets: Mobile operator customers in North America, Europe, Asia and other regions.
rationale: Niche B2B telecom supplier selling to operators, recently through a debt restructuring; weak F1 fit.
changed: Completed a debt restructuring in 2025

name: Momenta
desc: Develops driver-assistance and autonomous driving software for automakers, and robotaxi technology.
markets: Mainly Chinese car market, supplying domestic and foreign automakers; robotaxi plans in Europe with partners.
rationale: Automotive technology fit; Chinese Grand Prix and carmaker clients give some B2B angle.

name: Perplexity AI
desc: AI-powered answer engine and search company offering cited answers, Pro subscriptions, the Comet browser and an API.
markets: Users worldwide, with telecom distribution partnerships in several countries.
rationale: Consumer AI brand; rivals such as Anthropic and Google sponsor F1, giving strong technology fit.

name: Gen Digital
desc: Consumer cyber safety company selling Norton, Avast, AVG, LifeLock and Avira security, privacy and identity products.
markets: Consumer subscribers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, sold online and via partners.
rationale: Consumer security rivals Bitdefender and 1Password sponsor F1; strong consumer marketing fit.
changed: Formed in 2022 when NortonLifeLock merged with Avast; acquired MoneyLion in 2025

name: Oura Health
desc: Makes the Oura smart ring and app that track sleep, activity, heart rate and readiness.
markets: Consumers mainly in the US and Europe, with sales in other international markets.
rationale: Wellness wearable with sports partnerships; WHOOP already sponsors F1, showing a direct rival precedent.

name: Indra Sistemas (Indra Group)
desc: Defence and technology group making radar, air traffic, simulation and transport systems, plus Minsait IT consulting.
markets: Governments, militaries and companies in Spain, Europe, Latin America, Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Spanish technology champion; Madrid Grand Prix and engineering showcase fit, though defence exposure limits some activation.
f1: Possibly linked: F1 partner roster lists IndraMind, believed to be Indra's AI brand; not confirmed

name: OSL Group
desc: Digital asset financial services company offering licensed crypto exchange, brokerage, OTC trading and custody services.
markets: Mainly retail and institutional clients in Hong Kong under SFC licences; wider expansion not confirmed here.
rationale: Crypto exchanges such as OKX, Kraken and Crypto.com sponsor F1, but OSL is small and Hong Kong-focused.
changed: Renamed from BC Technology Group to OSL Group in 2024

name: OSL Group
desc: Digital asset financial services company offering licensed crypto exchange, brokerage, OTC trading and custody services.
markets: Mainly retail and institutional clients in Hong Kong under SFC licences; wider expansion not confirmed here.
rationale: Crypto exchanges such as OKX, Kraken and Crypto.com sponsor F1, but OSL is small and Hong Kong-focused.
changed: Renamed from BC Technology Group to OSL Group in 2024

name: Wasabi Technologies
desc: Sells low-cost S3-compatible cloud object storage to enterprises, media firms and managed service providers.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific served from data centres in those regions.
rationale: Cloud storage brand already active in sports sponsorship; F1 data and media storage showcase is plausible.

name: Omio
desc: Online travel booking platform comparing and selling train, bus, flight and ferry tickets from many providers.
markets: Mainly European travellers and routes, also covering North America and some other markets.
rationale: Consumer travel brand; European race travel offers activation, but marketing budget is modest.
changed: Renamed from GoEuro to Omio in 2019

name: Blockchain.com
desc: Crypto company offering a self-custody wallet, brokerage and exchange services, institutional trading and blockchain data.
markets: Retail and institutional users in many countries worldwide, subject to local licensing.
rationale: Crypto rivals such as Crypto.com, OKX and Kraken sponsor F1; consumer brand-building fit is strong.

name: OneFootball
desc: Football media platform offering scores, news, video and live match streaming through its app and website.
markets: Football fans mainly in Europe, plus Brazil, Mexico and other markets.
rationale: Football-focused media brand; content partnership possible, but F1 sponsorship is outside its core audience.

name: Datadog
desc: Observability and security platform providing monitoring, logs, application performance and security tools for cloud applications.
markets: About 30,000 customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Observability peers such as Dynatrace and Splunk sponsor F1; telemetry and monitoring showcase fits well.

name: Discord
desc: Voice, video and text chat platform for communities and friends, earning from Nitro subscriptions and advertising.
markets: Users worldwide, strongest in North America and Europe.
rationale: Young gaming audience overlaps with F1's growing fan base; community and esports activation fit.
changed: Reported to be preparing an IPO in 2025-26; listing status not confirmed

name: Wix.com
desc: Website-building platform letting small businesses and individuals create sites and online stores, with hosting and payments.
markets: Users in about 190 countries across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Heavy sports marketer; F1's global audience of small-business owners suits brand campaigns.
changed: Acquired Base44 in 2025

name: Samsung SDS
desc: IT services and logistics company providing cloud, system integration, AI, security and Cello Square logistics services.
markets: Mainly Samsung affiliates and Korean clients, with operations in the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Samsung affiliate with B2B focus; IT services peers sponsor F1, but marketing is largely group-led.

name: Brown & Brown
desc: Insurance brokerage placing property, casualty, employee benefits and specialty insurance for businesses and individuals.
markets: Mainly the United States, with operations in the UK, Ireland, Canada and other countries.
rationale: Broker rivals Aon and Marsh sponsor F1; B2B client hospitality case is clear.
changed: Acquired Accession Risk Management Group in 2025

name: Arcelik
desc: Manufactures home appliances and consumer electronics under brands such as Beko, Grundig, Arcelik, Blomberg and Defy.
markets: Sells in over 100 countries across Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa and the Middle East; factories in several countries.
rationale: Beko is an active sports sponsor; European consumer reach suits brand activation, moderate F1 fit.
changed: Formed Beko Europe with Whirlpool's European appliance business in 2024

name: Hopper
desc: Travel app predicting flight and hotel prices and selling bookings plus fintech add-ons and white-label travel services.
markets: Consumers mainly in North America; business division supplies travel platforms to partners abroad.
rationale: Travel brand with North American consumer reach; Canadian and US races give activation, but budget is uncertain.

name: Snyk
desc: Developer security platform scanning code, open-source dependencies, containers and cloud infrastructure for vulnerabilities.
markets: Software teams in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; development centres in London and Tel Aviv.
rationale: Cybersecurity peers sponsor F1; developer-focused brand with a moderate marketing budget and limited consumer need.

name: Neo4j
desc: Graph database company whose software analyses connected data for fraud detection, recommendations and AI knowledge graphs.
markets: Enterprise customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Data-platform peers sponsor F1; data showcase possible, though brand budget is limited.

name: Roblox Corporation
desc: Online platform where users create and play 3D games and experiences, earning from Robux virtual currency.
markets: Users worldwide, largest in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Young global audience; F1 brand experiences and virtual racing content fit, though Roblox rarely sponsors sport.

name: SS&C Technologies
desc: Provides investment accounting, fund administration and financial software and services to asset managers, banks and insurers.
markets: Clients and offices across the Americas, Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia.
rationale: Asset managers and banks value race hospitality; B2B client entertainment fit, with limited consumer marketing need.

name: ThoughtSpot
desc: Search- and AI-driven business intelligence software letting employees query and analyse company data in plain language.
markets: Enterprise customers mainly in North America and Europe, with offices in India.
rationale: Analytics peers such as Alteryx sponsor F1; data showcase fit but modest brand budget.

name: OVHcloud
desc: Cloud computing provider offering dedicated servers, hosting, public and private cloud from its own data centres.
markets: Mainly European customers, with data centres in North America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: European sovereign-cloud brand; technology showcase at European races plausible, but marketing spend is modest.

name: Workiva
desc: Cloud platform for financial reporting, ESG reporting, audit and compliance used by finance and risk teams.
markets: Mainly US enterprises, with customers in Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B finance-software brand; race hospitality for CFOs and audit leaders possible, weak-to-moderate fit.

name: Mapbox
desc: Mapping and location platform providing maps, navigation and search SDKs for apps and vehicles.
markets: Developers and automakers in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Automotive navigation customers give a mobility and in-car technology tie-in; small brand budget.

name: DeepL
desc: AI language company offering DeepL Translator, writing and voice tools to individuals and enterprises.
markets: Users and business customers worldwide, with offices in Europe, the US and Japan.
rationale: Multilingual F1 paddock and global audience fit translation story; growing enterprise brand.
changed: Grew out of Linguee and renamed DeepL in 2017

name: Pentera
desc: Automated security validation platform that simulates real attacks to find exploitable weaknesses for enterprises.
markets: Operations in the US, Germany, UK, Israel, Dubai and Singapore.
rationale: Cybersecurity peers sponsor F1, but Pentera's marketing budget is small; moderate fit for B2B hospitality.
changed: Renamed from Pcysys to Pentera

name: Motorola Solutions
desc: Provides land mobile radios, video security, command centre software and emergency call systems for public safety and enterprises.
markets: Government and enterprise customers in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Event security and critical communications fit race operations; B2B showcase to public safety buyers plausible.
changed: Formed in 2011 when Motorola Inc. split off Motorola Mobility

name: o9 Solutions
desc: Cloud planning software for demand, supply chain, revenue and integrated business planning at large companies.
markets: Consumer goods, retail and industrial customers in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Enterprise software peers sponsor F1; planning and AI showcase possible, modest brand scale.

name: Polygon Labs
desc: Develops Polygon blockchain networks and tools for scaling Ethereum, used by apps and brands for payments.
markets: Developers, crypto users and businesses worldwide; team distributed internationally.
rationale: Crypto peers sponsor F1, but Polygon's spending has been reduced; moderate fit.
changed: Launched as Matic Network, rebranded Polygon in 2021

name: MongoDB
desc: Database software company offering its document database as MongoDB Atlas cloud service and on-premises.
markets: Over 50,000 customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Data-platform peers such as Confluent sponsor F1; developer brand and technology showcase fit well.

name: PTC
desc: Industrial software company selling Creo CAD, Windchill product lifecycle management and Onshape to manufacturers.
markets: Manufacturing customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Engineering software used in motorsport; rivals Siemens and Synopsys (Ansys) are F1 partners.

name: Ziff Davis
desc: Digital media and internet company owning IGN, Mashable, PCMag, CNET, Everyday Health and Speedtest by Ookla.
markets: Audiences mainly in the US, with international editions and Ookla customers worldwide.
rationale: Tech and gaming media brands could offer content partnership; limited sponsor budget.
changed: Acquired CNET in 2024
